rules: Import `ruststream_kinesis::prelude::*` at a mount site; a handler body imports `ruststream::prelude::*` and bounds an injected slot with a capability, the one exception being a body that sets a record's partition key.
Name the stream by its name with `KinesisStream::new("orders")` inside `#[subscriber(..)]`; the bare `#[subscriber("orders")]` form builds the same descriptor with its default read settings.
Set `poll_interval(d)` and `create_if_missing(shards)` on the descriptor or at the mount site; on the mount chain they come after `batch(n)` and before `start_at(..)`, which replaces the descriptor.
Subscribe to a stream once per broker: a second subscription to the same stream on one broker is refused when it opens; a second `KinesisBroker` with a lease store of its own reads the stream again.
Key one record with `.partition_key(..)` on the publish builder, bounding the slot `Out<impl Publisher<Options = KinesisPublishOptions>, Marker>`.
Key every record of a position, a reply included, at the mount site: `.out_reply(Publish::default()).partition_key(..)`.

Cap redeliveries with `.max_attempts(n).dead_letter(stream)` after `include`; the framework publishes the copies back to the stream, each keeping its partition key and arriving at the tip of its shard.
Where order matters, declare no cap and return `HandlerOutcome::retry()`: the shard's checkpoint stops at the record, and the shard is read again from it when its lease is next taken.
Treat `ack` as a per-shard checkpoint: it moves only when every earlier record of the shard is handled, `HandlerOutcome::drop()` retires a poison record, and delivery is at-least-once.
Keep checkpoints in `MemoryLeaseStore` (the default) for one instance; give several instances one `DynamoLeaseStore` table (feature `dynamodb-lease`) with a string partition key `lease_key`.
Leave `owner_id` out so each broker takes a unique id, or give each instance a stable name of its own; never share one fixed id between two instances running at the same time.
Build the broker with `KinesisBroker::from_config(config)` when the service loads its own AWS config, as a `DynamoLeaseStore` needs; set endpoint, region and credentials on that config.
Read a `DynamoDB` lease table an earlier version keyed by bare shard id through `DynamoLeaseStore::legacy_stream(stream)`, naming the one stream those rows belong to.

Open or move a subscription with `KinesisPosition`: `start_at(..)` for the shards it opens with, `Ctx<SeekHandle>` in a handler; a stream-wide position moves every shard, `sequence` only the shard it names.

Test a service by handing the app `main` runs to `ruststream::testing::TestApp::start`, which connects `KinesisBroker` in process with the `testing` feature, and address it as `tb.broker::<KinesisBroker>()`.
Run the in-process test body against LocalStack or AWS with `TestApp::start_live` for what only the service has: shards, leases, checkpoints, retention and resharding.
